title: Ensemble Methods: Bagging
description: Breiman's bagging trains models on bootstrap resamples and averages their votes; variance falls while bias holds. The council's simplest form: many weak judges, one robust verdict.

demo.code:
import random
random.seed(1001)
n=200; p=0.62
# Council of 5 independent reasoners, each correct with prob p, majority vote
truth=[random.random()<0.5 for _ in range(n)]
correct=0
for t in truth:
    v=sum(1 for _ in range(5) if random.random()<p)
    maj=v>=3
    if maj==t: correct+=1
acc=correct/n
import math
# Condorcet majority accuracy for odd m=5
m=5
cond=sum(math.comb(m,k)*(p**k)*((1-p)**(m-k)) for k in range(3,6))
print(f"n=200 individual_p={p:.2f} majority_acc={acc:.3f} condorcet_theory={cond:.3f}")
print("DEMO_OK")
demo.note: Runnable demo program verified by execution during the database build.

architecture: Bootstrap resamples feed independent learners; predictions aggregate by vote or average. Out-of-bag samples provide a free performance estimate.
implementation_status: Public method, established (Breiman 1996). Prototype validated in this build (executed 2026-10-21).
provenance: Breiman, L. (1996). Bagging predictors. Machine Learning. Public record.
